media:group.media:title: Live - ECB Annual Research Conference 2026 (Day 2)
media:group.media:description:
- Geoeconomics and the International Trading System - 16 and 17 September 2026, Frankfurt am Main, Germany.
The rules-based multilateral international trading system is under strain. Great-power competition, security concerns, and the deliberate use of geoeconomic dependencies for strategic ends point towards a fundamental shift in the relationship between economics and geopolitics. This year's Annual Research Conference wants to contribute to a better understanding of the underlying dynamics by showcasing the latest academic research and by providing a forum for researchers and policymakers to exchange ideas and discuss Europe's options in this new global environment.
The conference will be live-streamed.
Programme: https://www.ecb.europa.eu/press/conferences/html/20260916_11th_ecb_annual_research_conference.en.html
- 09:51 - Jean Monnet lecture “Economic Size and Economic Power” Paul Krugman, City University of New York Chair: Philip R. Lane, Member of the Executive Board, European Central Bank
- 1:53:56 - Session 3 The Welfare Effects of Sanctions and Tariffs Chair: Isabel Vansteenkiste, Principal Counsellor, European Central Bank
A World Trading System for Whom? Evidence from Global Tariffs • Rodrigo Adão, University of Chicago Booth School of Business • John Sturm Becko, Princeton University • Arnaud Costinot*, Massachusetts Institute of Technology • Dave Donaldson, Massachusetts Institute of Technology Discussant: Meredith Crowley, University of Cambridge

entry.title: What 25 years in central banking teach you – In Conversation with Boris Vujčić

media:group.media:title: What 25 years in central banking teach you – In Conversation with Boris Vujčić
media:group.media:description:
He’s spent over two decades in central banking, helped lead Croatia into the euro area and is now the ECB’s Vice-President.
In this episode of In Conversation, Boris Vujčić joins our host Stefania Secola to reflect on the experiences that shaped him, discuss European financial stability and share his top priorities for his new role.
The views expressed are those of the speakers and not necessarily those of the European Central Bank.
